investigations.discriminator: Pending: the per-mode successor execution, which should turn comparison 0 and comparison 1 from `unknown` into decisive results (control holds, mode B holds) while leaving comparison 2 violated. Still open and unmeasured: whether the same false success is reachable without the tick race - e.g. with a follower as the origin (assignment arriving through the leader's `Assigned` reply), with batch_size > 1, or with a flexible quorum - and whether an origin that reads the decided log at the returned index can still be misled by a value that matches but is not its entry.

knowledge.statement: The repository's own caller of `append_notify` treats a successful resolution as synchronous durability confirmation of that specific entry and announces the returned index without re-reading the log at it: `examples/kv_store_async/src/main.rs` documents `append_notify` as being for "a specific entry whose durability the caller must confirm synchronously ... the entry is decided at its assigned index", and after `append_notify(quota).await?` it prints "quota entry durably decided at log idx {idx}, safe to announce". The existing runtime test for the same call asserts only that the returned index is non-zero and that the decided suffix is non-empty, so no in-repo test pins the entry actually occupying the returned index.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to callers that follow the documented/example pattern of treating `Ok(idx)` as confirmation for their own entry at `idx` without reading the decided log at that index. Under the mode-C interleaving of the retained executions (leader partitioned, entry accepted locally, new leader decides a different entry at the same index, origin re-synchronized) that pattern turns the false success into an announced write that is not in the decided log.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. `append_notify` assignments carry only `(log index, ballot at assignment)`, and the success arm of `drain_notifiers` fires on `assigned_idx <= local decided index` alone, before the ballot-change arm and without comparing the caller's entry with what occupies that index; both receipts of this experiment show the consequence on real actor instances. In mode C the origin was the leader, was cut off from both followers, and took entry 11 while partitioned (its decided index stayed 0 throughout, so the entry was accepted but nothing advanced), whereupon node 3 won the election among the followers and decided entry 22 at log index 1. After the origin was reconnected and re-synchronized, its call for entry 11 resolved `ok` with assigned index 1 while the decided entry at index 1 was 22 and the origin's entire decided log was `22` - entry 11 exists in no decided log. The corrected execution's own comparison machinery now states this: the comparison whose predicate is 'if the resolution is Ok then the decided entry at the returned index is the caller's entry' is evaluated `violated` with valid witness index 9 and a complete witness (its control and mode-B counterparts were evaluated but could not be completed because all three cases shared one result event name; that selection defect is corrected in the successor run submitted here). The same call under the control condition resolved `ok` with entry 11 genuinely at index 1, so the signal is meaningful when the entry survives; and the identical lost-entry state with 2 ms ticks resolved the documented `Superseded` at event index 5. Which signal the caller gets is thus decided by whether the origin's promise change and its decided-index advance happen to fall inside one tick period, not by the durable outcome of the write. The caller-facing consequence is sourced in this repository: the async example documents `append_notify` as confirming durability synchronously for a specific entry 'decided at its assigned index' and announces the returned index without re-reading the log there, while the existing runtime test only asserts a non-zero index and a non-empty suffix - so this defect is both reachable and relied upon by the shipped usage pattern, and no existing test pins the entry at the returned index. Claim is scoped to this actor layer, this fault model (whole-message loss plus election-timeout takeover), batch_size 1 and a majority quorum.
counterevidence: The entry-point documentation of `append_notify` promises only to resolve "when the assigned log index is decided" and, for Superseded, advises re-reading the returned index; read that way `Ok(idx)` is a claim about the index and not about the caller's value, so a caller that verifies the entry at the returned index is not misled. This weakens the caller-facing consequence but not the schedule dependence, since one durable lost-entry state cannot legitimately yield both `Superseded` and `Ok` if the signal describes state rather than timing.

A new leader must adopt any value a majority-overlapping write quorum already accepted, so an entry that reached a write quorum cannot be replaced; the loss needs a local-only assignment, which the retained events support (origin decided index 0 while partitioned, the new leader's event reporting entry 22 decided at index 1, and the new leader's decided values `22` only).

The `Superseded` arm does not confirm the caller's entry either; it stops waiting. The two arms differ in what they claim, and the defect is that the optimistic claim can be delivered for the same state.

In both receipts the controller's comparisons for the control and mode-B cases were `unknown` (missing_indices include the other modes' events) although each evaluated its own event; that incompleteness is an artifact of my shared result event name, not contrary evidence about the behaviour.
limitations: In-process in-memory transport, no crash or restart: the origin is re-synchronized from the new leader, not recovered from storage, so nothing here extends to the persistence/fail-recovery path.

One cluster shape and one fault pattern (both directions of the old leader's links dropped, election-timeout takeover, batch_size 1, majority quorum, the second entry appended through the new leader). Follower-origin assignments, batching above 1 and flexible quorums are unmeasured.

The schedule dependence is characterised by two tick periods only (2 ms and 80 ms) around a round trip of about 2-4 ms; it bounds neither the deployment frequency of the false success nor the exact tick/RTT threshold.
The per-mode successor execution is submitted in this update; until its receipt exists, the control and mode-B comparisons remain `unknown` in the evaluated set even though their events were parsed.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts come from the same experiment lineage: 7fe56f0c8c6745a18e94af7244e746b9-experiment is the revision of 51798029045d462699a54d5065e069eb-experiment whose only difference is that the admission events carry the identity fields (difference_fields: harness, prefix), and both were executed from the same scenario steps, tick periods, comparisons and applicability: cases A/B/C passed in both, and the three cited events agree field for field in both runs (mode A: resolved ok, assigned_idx 1, entry_at_assigned_idx decided:11; mode B: resolved superseded, assigned_idx 1, origin decided index 0; mode C: resolved ok, assigned_idx 1, entry_at_assigned_idx decided:22, entry_equals_submitted false, origin decided values 22, origin decided index 0 while partitioned). The v1 receipt contributes the parsed events (its comparisons were unevaluable because the admissions lacked identity); the v2 receipt contributes the same events plus the evaluated comparison that is `violated` with valid witness index 9. No preprocessing, scenario or measurement difference exists between the two receipts beyond the emitted admission fields and the evaluation of the comparison chain.

scope.description: One real in-process cluster shape (three OmniPaxos actors over an in-memory transport, majority quorum, batch_size 1, node 1 forced into the leader role), run three times with different admissions, each case emitting its result under its own event name. Mode A (control): no partition, so entry 11 appended through the origin is replicated and decided normally. Modes B and C: node 1's links to both followers are cut in both directions, node 1 - still the leader in the accept phase - takes entry 11 (so it can only be accepted locally and assigned an index), the two followers elect node 3, which decides entry 22 at the same first index, and node 1 is then reconnected so the new leader re-synchronizes it. B and C differ only in the actor tick period (2 ms vs 80 ms), which controls whether a drain_notifiers pass can run between the origin's promise change and its decided-index advance.
assumptions: Message loss/partition is a permitted fault for this protocol; the core tolerates lost messages via its resend path, and the harness drops whole messages inside the transport without adding backpressure.
Each node is a real OmniPaxos instance with MemoryStorage, batch_size 1 and a majority quorum, driven only through the public actor handle; no target logic is modified.

Node 1 carries leader_priority 1 so the pre-partition leader is stable; a higher priority only breaks ties at equal ballot number, and in modes B/C the followers reach a strictly higher ballot number through the election-timeout takeover path.

drain_notifiers runs only from the tick branch, so the resolution instant is quantised by tick_period; the gap between the origin's Prepare handling and the AcceptSync that follows it is one round trip (about 2-4 ms here).
excluded: Any claim about entries other than the two submitted values (11 by the origin, 22 by the new leader).
Any claim about transports, runtimes or timings other than the in-process in-memory transport used here.
Durable/crash recovery: the origin is re-synchronized in-process, it is not restarted, so no storage-persistence claim follows from these cases.

experiment.prefix: Per case: build three OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..3, configuration_id 1, nodes [1,2,3], MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, election_tick_timeout 3, node 1 leader_priority 1) and spawn each as an actor through spawn_actor with a tokio-backed AsyncRuntime adapter (tick_period per case, egress_period 1 ms). Wire every node's outgoing_messages() receiver into a task that consults a per-direction block set and, unless the link is blocked, delivers the message with peer.handle_incoming(). Admission: call handles[1].try_become_leader() until all three nodes report current_leader() == (1, true) and still do so after four election timeouts; emit the admission event carrying mode, cluster setup, origin 1, submitted_value 11 and the tick period. Mode A: await handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)) and then read the origin's decided suffix, emitting the result as `notify_resolution_a`. Modes B/C: block (1,2) and (1,3) both ways, spawn handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)) as a task, sleep one tick period, wait until nodes 2 and 3 both report a leader other than 1 with accepted=true, await handles[new_leader].append_notify(TestEntry(22)), then unblock both links and await the origin's future, emitting the result as `notify_resolution_b` or `notify_resolution_c` respectively. Every result event carries the resolved variant (ok / superseded / timeout / ...), the assigned index, the decided entry at that index and, only when that index was actually observed in the decided log, whether it equals the submitted value.
semantic_changes: Cases A, B and C share one invocation and are separated by admission only: A has no partition, B and C use the identical partition and differ solely in tick_ms (2 vs 80).
Each case emits its result under a mode-specific event name and each comparison selects its own case's name; measured quantities and assertions are unchanged from the previous revision.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs are produced by the target itself: the actor assigns the caller's entry an index from its own local accept as leader, records the assignment as (index, ballot) with no entry identity, and drain_notifiers derives the resolution from the local decided index alone, evaluating the Ok arm before the ballot-change arm. The caller supplies only the entry value.

comparisons.description: Control: without a partition the success resolution names an index whose decided entry is the caller's entry.
Same lost-entry setup with a 2 ms tick: the documented heuristic resolution is the one delivered.

Same lost-entry setup with an 80 ms tick: if the resolution is Ok, the returned index must hold the caller's entry. A false value is the violating witness; if mode C resolves anything else, the antecedent does not hold and the assertion is not applicable.

experiment.revision_reason: Comparison-selection correction only: each case now emits its result under a mode-specific event name (`notify_resolution_a` / `notify_resolution_b` / `notify_resolution_c`) and the three comparisons select those names, so each comparison sees exactly one result event and can be evaluated complete against its own admission. In the previous revision all cases shared the event name `notify_resolution`, which left comparisons 0 and 1 `unknown` (`No corresponding prerequisite events reached: admission_a/admission` at the mode B and C events) although each comparison's own event was evaluated. Scenarios, tick periods, assertions, antecedents and applicability are unchanged; a fresh execution is required because the harness bytes and the comparison event selectors changed.
